texts.preamble: Mohd. Abbas Sheikh vs Union Territory Of J&K & Ors on 1 January, 2025 Author: Sindhu Sharma Bench: Sindhu Sharma Sr. No. 52 High Court Of Jammu & Kashmir And Ladakh At Jammu Wp(C) No. 06/2025 Mohd. Abbas Sheikh .... Petitioner/Appellant(s) Through:- Mr. Sumir Pandita, Advocate V/s Union Territory of J&K & ors. .....Respondent(s) Through:- Mrs. Monika Kohli, Sr. Aag Coram : Hon'Ble Mrs. Justice Sindhu Sharma, Judge Order 01.01.2025 01.
texts.facts: The petitioner is proprietor of M/s Furqaan Traders and M/s Sheikh Traders situated at Rajeev Nagar Narwal. They are registered under J&K Shops and Establishment Act, 1966 to deal in sale of small animals skin. The business of the petitioner is also registered with the department of Health and Medical Education Food Safety and Standards Authority of India. This was stopped by the petitioner when the business of the petitioner was sealed by respondent No. 2. Thereafter the petitioner furnished an undertaking that he will not process the livestock shop nor hold the same. The petitioner is conducting the business as per registration certificates. The respondents have unnecessarily started harassing the petitioner and asked to close the same.
texts.arguments: 02. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is using the shops as go down for his livestock and hides of the animals and the petitioner was also running the same for processing the livestock. Mrs. Monika Kohli, learned Sr. AAG accepts notice on behalf of respondents and states that she has no objection if this petition is disposed of by directing the respondents not to interfere in the aforesaid business of the petitioner.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 02. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is using the shops as go down for his livestock and hides of the animals and the petitioner was also running the same for processing the livestock. Mrs. Monika Kohli, learned Sr. AAG accepts notice on behalf of respondents and states that she has no objection if this petition is disposed of by directing the respondents not to interfere in the aforesaid business of the petitioner.
